ovincial online gaming operator.
Fortunately for Canadians, the lack of regulation does not mean it is illegal to gamble at online casinos. While unregulated casinos do not pay taxes to the provincial governments and cannot legally establish a presence here, there are no laws preventing Canadians from playing at these sites online. Similar to shopping online at an overseas retailer, the money spent at a grey-market casino simply leaves the Canadian economy.
Additionally, many online casinos will receive a license from the Kahnawake Gaming Commission in Canada, which certifies them as trustworthy and safe.
Ontario iGaming Regulation
Ontario is the only exception to the grey-market laws mentioned above, as they are the single province today that regulates sports betting and online casino operators. Online casinos that wish to operate within Ontario must meet strict regulatory compliance rules to receive a license.
These casinos also pay taxes to the government of Ontario. For players, regulation rules mean they can rest assured that the casinos they're using are legitimate and care enough about player safety to abide by the rules established.
Responsible Gambling in CA
Legitimate online casinos take responsible gambling seriously and often offer resources to players to prevent problem gambling. Players should always take the time to set up deposit and loss limits, which ensure they stay within their set limits. Other types of limits include logged-in time limits and a logged-in time block, which both limit the number of hours spent at an online casino. Alternatively, players can set spend and wager limits, preventing them from playing more, even if they're winning.
Players should take the time to learn about gambling addiction and how to identify the signs in themselves and others. Most online casinos will have a section on responsible gaming in the footer of their website, where players can access resources like videos, articles, and courses to learn more about gambling addiction. Understanding these signs and symptoms can help keep yourself, minors, and loved ones safe.
CA Gambling Tools
Here are a few more responsible gambling tools available in Canada:
- CAMH: The Centre of Addiction and Mental Health, Canada's largest mental health teaching hospital, advocates for addiction prevention. Individuals who feel they need help stepping away from gambling can phone the referrals department at +1 416 535 8501 ext. 2 to seek help.
- Gamblers Anonymous: Proven to be an effective method in treating addiction, GA is a community driven by a desire to stop gambling. Free to join for anyone, GA hosts several meetings nationwide that individuals can attend to discuss and seek support in their experience.
- GamblingTherapy.org: GamblingTherapy.org is a free site that offers support and resources to problem gamblers seeking help. The site provides advice for friends and family of problem gamblers, in addition to support forums, articles, resources, and quizzes.
